newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Japan's June tankan survey.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Bank of Japan's June tankan survey.

text.p: Below is a selection of economists' and analysts' reactions to the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "tankan" quarterly corporate survey in June, released on Wednesday, which showed that the business outlook among major manufacturers had improved since the previous survey in March.
YASUSHI OKADA, SENIOR ECONOMIST, INVESTMENT ADVISORY DEPARTMENT, DAIWA SECURITIES CO:

"The tankan data confirmed that Japan's economic structure has not changed at all. Japan, despite its international pledge to achieve domestic demand-led growth, is still heavily dependant on major manufacturers, or more specifically, exporting industries.
Meanwhile, a weak outlook for non-manufacturers and smaller enterprises, promises that the Bank of Japan will hold down ultra low interest rates for a while."
JANE BERRYMAN, SENIOR ANALYST, TECHNICAL DATA, TOKYO:
"To say the report is an eye-popper is an understatement. Not only did the headline number for June come in higher than expected, but the forecast for September was equally a jawdropper.
"What we're going to have on our hands is basically an unwinding of all the gains we priced in (in JGBs) on Monday and Tuesday."

"It's highly likely we could see a rate rise in the latter half of the year, probably the fourth quarter, if we get a confirmation of today's message in the September tankan itself. Clearly it's stronger than we thought...you have to move forward expectations of a tightening of credit."
